mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10Y-2Y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, exceeding a 0.5% month-over-month decline, signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle with input disruptions and rising costs.
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a triggered INDPRO decline, indicating the market is shrugging off the supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate, especially if the 3-month change exceeds 0.3 percentage points, signals a weakening labor market that will drag on consumer spending and pressure S&P 500 returns lower over the next month.
failure_condition: Retail sales (RSAFS) and consumer sentiment indices show no concurrent weakening, suggesting the rising unemployment is not impacting consumer behavior.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that will slow economic growth and weigh on S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Leading economic indicators like the yield curve and manufacturing PMIs remain at expansionary levels, indicating the Fed's tightening has not yet slowed the real economy.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) both show year-over-year growth exceeding 5%, it signals a broad-based consumer-led economic upswing that will boost S&P 500 returns over the next quarter.
failure_condition: The composite PMI index falls below 50, indicating a concurrent contraction in the manufacturing and services sectors that will offset the consumer strength.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 300,000 jobs in a month, it signals a blowout labor market report that will boost S&P 500 returns over the next week as the market prices in stronger growth.
failure_condition: The labor force participation rate declines sharply in the same report, indicating that the job growth is being driven by a temporary surge in labor supply rather than demand.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% year-over-year, and the Fed funds rate is below 2%, it signals an inflation overshoot that the market expects the Fed to address with aggressive rate hikes, pressuring S&P 500 returns lower over the next month.
failure_condition: The Fed signals a more dovish stance than expected, or market-based inflation expectations (e.g., 5y5y forwards) decline, indicating the inflation spike is seen as transitory.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) both decline simultaneously over a 3-month period, it signals a supply-driven growth slowdown that will weigh on S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Commodity prices and shipping costs decline sharply, indicating that the supply constraints are easing and growth is poised to rebound.
